title_original: Latino Film Institute Names Seventh Annual Inclusion Fellowship Cohort
excerpt_original: The Latino Film Institute has unveiled its seventh annual cohort of directors for the LFI Inclusion Fellowship supported by Netflix. Ten emerging filmmakers join the program to produce live-action narrative short films through $50,000 production grants, mentorship and industry…

blocks.text: The Latino Film Institute has unveiled its seventh annual cohort of directors for the LFI Inclusion Fellowship supported by Netflix.

Ten emerging filmmakers join the program to produce live-action narrative short films through $50,000 production grants, mentorship and industry engagement opportunities. Fellows participate in a studio-style environment and will screen their completed films at the Los Angeles Latino International Film Festival.

blocks.text: “Netflix’s continued commitment to the LFI Inclusion Fellowship makes a real difference for filmmakers with bold, original stories to tell,” said Diana Cadavid, director of industry programs at the Latino Film Institute. “This year’s cohort spans horror, coming-of-age, comedy, romance, sci-fi and drama and every project stands out for its visual ambition and conceptual strength. Through mentorship, resources and direct industry access, we’re supporting the selected filmmakers to bring their visions to the screen and opening doors for the advancement of their careers.”

The fellows will also participate in LALIFF Connect: Market & Creative Forum, the festival’s professional development and networking section. There, the cohort will be able to network with industry professionals in production, distribution, acquisitions and representation.

The 2027 LFI cohort is: Adalberto Angulo — “Saboteur” Alexander Ibarra — “Mariposa Muere” Berman Fenelus — “The Last Hive” Camila de Ilhéus — “d’Aparecida” Crystal Ferreiro — “PUMPED!” Jasmin Prophete — “Zonbi” Kevin Rios — “Hurricane Mima” María Sofía Hernández — “El Turno (Carpool)” Mariales Diaz — “Tío dice que te suelte en banda (Don’t Hold Me Close)” Miguel Ortiz — “Brother Bushi”
Since forming, the fellowship has launched 55 alumni in producing films that have premiered at major festivals and secured distribution.
